intro: Singapore is a small, flat, tropical island at the tip of the Malay Peninsula, made bigger by land reclaimed from the sea.

chapters.title: A growing island
text: The main island and over 60 small islets cover about 735 km², around a quarter more than in 1965 thanks to land reclamation. The highest point, Bukit Timah, is only 163 m.
The Johor Strait separates it from Malaysia, crossed by a causeway.

chapters.title: City in a garden
text: Despite being crowded, Singapore keeps rainforest reserves, parks and the Gardens by the Bay with giant 'Supertrees'.

keyTerms.meaning: Making new land by filling in the sea.
